events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
The rider's complaint alleges both overcharging and feeling unsafe, so the safety screen (SAFE-1) must be read first [F7][F8]. The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped [F9]; the rider asked why they were going that way at 09:03 [F7], and the driver replied "Shut up and let me drive." at 09:04 [F8]. Read in context this is not a route instruction or a pickup arrangement: it is hostile, dismissive language aimed at the rider who was questioning the route, and Ryde's code of conduct bars abuse of any kind under SAFE-1. This makes the safety screen at least "suspected" for abuse/harassment, and a suspected safety concern requires the case to go to a human instead of a keyword-free automatic refund [F7][F8][SAFE-1].

On the route questions: the trace already settles that one off-route segment exists [F3][RD-1] and that no qualifying traffic incident excuses it — the speed-band facts on PIE and KPE are band 4 and stand alone, so RD-4(b) cannot exempt [F11][F12][F13][RD-4]. Nothing in the chat shows a rider message before 08:58:30 agreeing to any road, area or route the driver named; the only pre-segment content in the record is absent and the driver's post-trip statement that his GPS rerouted him is a claim, not rider consent [F3][F9][F10][RD-5]. Nor is there any rider-requested named stop in the segment, so RD-3(a) does not apply [F3][RD-3]. The segment therefore counts [F3].

The distance actually driven was 20.1 km against an optimal 15.9 km [F1], and the off-route segment added 3.75 km [F3]. Since this is a metered RydeTAXI trip, refundable mileage is Σ(extra_km) × per-km rate [RD-2]: rate = $28.30 ÷ 20.1 km = $1.4080/km [F6], so 3.75 km × $1.4080 = $5.28 [F3][F4][F6][RD-2]. That is the amount a human should release if the safety review clears the case; the case does not meet RD-6 because the driver has no prior upheld route dispute in 90 days, so no account flag [F16][RD-6].

No flag has been added to your account for this. We can't say how long the review will take, but we'll let you know. You don't need to do anything.
